short: The 'Sailor King' whose brief reign saw the passing of the transformative Great Reform Act.
full:
Succeeding his brother George IV in 1830 at the age of 64, William IV brought a more modest and informal style to the monarchy after his career in the Royal Navy. He inherited a political landscape fractured by demands for parliamentary reform, and his reign was almost immediately consumed by the profound constitutional crisis surrounding the Reform Bill.

Although initially reluctant, William's eventual agreement to create enough new Whig peers to force the bill through the House of Lords ensured its passage in 1832. This monumental legislation swept away 'rotten boroughs' and expanded the electorate, fundamentally shifting political power towards the growing industrial middle classes and preventing widespread civil unrest.
